jobs.description:
About Gusto 

 At Gusto, we're on a mission to grow the small business economy. We handle the hard stuff — payroll, health insurance, 401(k)s, and HR — so owners can focus on their craft and their customers. With teams in Denver, San Francisco, and New York, we support more than 500,000 small businesses nationwide and are building a workplace that reflects the people we serve.

 
All full-time employees receive competitive base pay, benefits, and equity (RSUs) — because everyone who helps build Gusto should share in its success. Offer amounts are determined by role, level, and location. Learn more about our Total Rewards philosophy .

 
AI is a fundamental part of how work gets done at Gusto. We expect all team members to actively engage with AI tools relevant to their role and grow their fluency as the technology evolves. AI experience requirements vary by role and will be assessed during the interview process.

 About Design at Gusto 
 Design at Gusto is made up of over 80 creative, collaborative people who care deeply about our mission to empower small businesses and their employees. We're a cross-functional group that is always looking for opportunities to build understanding and empathy for the people who use Gusto. We don't care much about swim lanes and though we care deeply about quality and craft, we are never precious about it. We work closely with cross-functional partners in Product, Engineering, Data, and Marketing to design, build, and ship experiences that make a real difference.

 We are building an AI-native design organization — and we mean that seriously. We're looking for designers who are already working this way: using AI to prototype ideas quickly, shorten customer feedback loops, and ship quality UX directly to customers.

 About the Role 
 Gusto's Growth team owns the full customer funnel — from a small business's first visit to gusto.com through onboarding and into ongoing expansion. Two of the most complex, cross-cutting systems inside that funnel are how we price and package our products, and how we orchestrate the messages customers get across email, sales, and in-product surfaces. Neither has ever had dedicated, systems-level design support until now.

 This role is leveled at the equivalent to a Staff-level. As Product Designer in this scope, you'll own the design system for how promotions, tiers, and SKUs are presented consistently across the funnel, including a unified checkout experience, and drive the next wave of iteration following our fall pricing & packaging refresh. Alongside that, you'll partner closely with our Revenue Systems team to define the target-state UX vision for customer-centric orchestration: establishing how a customer experiences one coordinated set of communications across email, sales, and in-product/AI surfaces, rather than a patchwork of independent touchpoints, and drawing the line between what belongs at the platform level versus the channel level. You'll round this out with lighter-touch, ongoing design support for Invoicing & Billing as needs arise, including near-term work like multi-entity billing.

 This is a systems-thinking role, with direct impact on revenue generation. You'll need to be as comfortable zooming out to define a multi-team experience architecture as you are zooming in to get the details of a specific surface right, and you'll need a strong customer experience and business sensibility to match.

 About the team 
 Gusto's Growth team is dedicated to helping customers discover, adopt, and expand into the Gusto ecosystem in meaningful ways. You'll be joining a collaborative, cross-functional team of designers, engineers, PMs, data scientists, and key business partners who care deeply about customer experience — and who operate at the intersection of product-led growth, marketing, and sales. In this role, you'll work closely with partners across Growth & Commerce, Revenue Systems, Sales, Marketing, and BizTech, while serving as the lead designer across several interrelated surfaces and systems.

 Here's what you'll do day-to-day: 
 

• Design dynamic pricing and packaging displays that span the funnel—from acquisition through activation and billing to ensure that buyers will quickly and confidently purchase Gusto products. 

• Design across Gusto's invoicing and billing surfaces, building on the recently rebuilt IBEX platform 

• Build and improve internal tools such as the Promo Engine and Product Catalog, and improve existing workflows in Gusto's internal platforms, to enable self-service and better outcomes for internal teams across Growth, Marketing, Accounting, Sales, and Expansion Sales. 

• Partner with Revenue Systems to define the target-state UX vision for multi-channel messaging orchestration—establishing systems cohesion across email, sales, and in-product/AI surfaces, and standardizing how AI-driven messaging is structured, sequenced, and represented to customers. 

• Draw the line between what belongs at the platform level versus the channel level (e.g., AI Email, Rec Center, Gus) so each surface stops solving the same problems separately. 

• Drive holistic service design, connecting the dots between how internal teams support customer decisions and how customers experience pricing, billing, and messaging throughout their journey. 

• Collaborate deeply with cross-functional partners to align on strategy, lead workshops, and co-create end-to-end solutions across multiple surfaces. 

• Create scalable, consistent patterns by working with and contributing to Gusto's design system to ensure alignment across internal and external experiences. 

• Use a mix of data and qualitative insights to validate decisions, inform tradeoffs, and refine designs over time through iteration. 
 
 Here's what we're looking for: 
 

• 8+ years of product design experience with a strong portfolio of systems-level design, internal tooling, and customer-facing product surfaces. 

• Experience working on complex, data-rich products—particularly in B2B SaaS environments with interconnected product offerings. 

• Demonstrated success in designing for both internal users and external customers, and the ability to balance their competing needs. 

• Fluency in UX best practices, UI design, interaction design, and accessibility standards. 

• Strong service design capabilities and a proven ability to map and simplify complex systems across touchpoints and orgs. 

• Experience designing for multi-channel systems cohesion—unifying messaging, sequencing, and experience across email, sales, and in-product/AI surfaces—and a point of view on standardizing AI-driven messaging at scale. 

• Excellent collaboration and communication skills, with the ability to lead through influence and align cross-functional teams. 

• Comfort leading ambiguous, 0-to-1 work, and building long-term vision while executing toward near-term milestones. 

• Experience using tools like Figma, Amplitude, and FullStory—and in leveraging mixed-methods research to inform design. 

• Passion for empowering internal teams and improving the quality of internal systems through intuitive, scalable design. 
 
 Our cash compensation range for this role is $147,000/yr to $183,000/yr in Denver, and $177,000/yr to $222,000/yr in San Francisco and New York. Final offer amounts are determined by multiple factors, including candidate experience and expertise, and may vary from the amounts listed above.

 
 Gusto has physical office spaces in Denver, San Francisco, and New York City. Employees who are based in those locations will be expected to work from the office on designated days approximately 2-3 days per week (or more depending on role). The same office expectations apply to all Symmetry roles, Gusto's subsidiary, whose physical office is in Scottsdale. 

 Note: The San Francisco office expectations encompass both the San Francisco and San Jose metro areas. 

 When approved to work from a location other than a Gusto office, a secure, reliable, and consistent internet connection is required. This includes non-office days for hybrid employees.

 
 Our customers come from all walks of life and so do we. We hire great people from a wide variety of backgrounds, not just because it's the right thing to do, but because it makes our company stronger. If you share our values and our enthusiasm for small businesses, you will find a home at Gusto. 

 Gusto is proud to be an equal opportunity employer. We do not discriminate in hiring or any employment decision based on race, color, religion, national origin, age, sex (including pregnancy, childbirth, or related medical conditions), marital status, ancestry, physical or mental disability, genetic information, veteran status, gender identity or expression, sexual orientation, or other applicable legally protected characteristic. Gusto considers qualified applicants with criminal histories, consistent with applicable federal, state and local law. Gusto is also committed to providing reasonable accommodations for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in our job application procedures. We want to see our candidates perform to the best of their ability. If you require a medical or religious accommodation at any time throughout your candidate journey, please fill out this form and a member of our team will get in touch with you.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 About the role 
 Prompts spec out what Claude does. Evals measure whether it did. The Product Prompt and Eval Design team does both for product design: the system prompt that greets a new user, the tool descriptions that decide whether Claude searches, the instructions that keep a slide deck from tipping into slop, and the evals that test all of it. The point is to keep the model and the product aligned with what users expect, what the product strategy calls for, and what safety requires, on every surface and through every model launch.

 This role is a foundational member of that work on the eval side: building the evals that check the prompts, the harness that runs them, and the tools that let designers do this work themselves. It sits on the Product Prompt and Eval Design team in Product Design, works day to day with the team's surface owners and the engineers in each product team, and pairs per surface with the prompt engineering team at model releases.

 Key responsibilities 
 

• Write and revise the prompts behind Claude's tools, features, and behaviors on a product surface; test the surface, turn findings into prompt fixes, ship them, and confirm the prompt users get is the one intended 

• Build the graders that prove a prompt fix and rerun on the next model; turn designers' hand-run rubrics into automated evals, then read transcripts for what the eval missed 

• Build visual, low-code eval tools designers can use without an engineer: assemble a comparison set from real transcripts, turn a plain-English rubric into a grader, compare prompt variants across models side by side, and read results in the tool rather than a notebook 

• Watch designers use those tools and make them simpler 

• Support model releases: test each surface against the new model, write prompt fixes and migrations, and write prompts for features launching with it, so the surface owner's call has numbers behind it 

• Stand up and scale the eval harness: build the test environment that exercises our 50 to 100 tools with trustworthy settings, keep evals green across models, and call whether a regression is the harness or the model 

• Package what prompting can't fix for training, with the eval attached: graders for crisp behaviors, human-feedback questions and good/bad pairs for fuzzy ones like writing quality 
 
 Minimum qualifications 
 

• Production-quality Python 

• Experience building and maintaining evaluation pipelines for LLM products: graders, rubrics, comparison sets, regression suites, and the plumbing that runs them across models 

• Experience building internal tools with a real interface for people who do not write code 

• Experience standing up test harnesses, sandboxing tool calls, and pinning the settings that make runs comparable 

• Experience shipping prompts, or working closely with people who do, and understanding why a prompt that works on one model fails on the next 

• Reads transcripts, not only scores 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Has worked inside a model-launch cycle 

• A/B testing experience and the ability to connect offline evals to online outcomes 

• Front-end or notebook-to-app experience, and opinions about what makes an eval result legible at a glance 

• Has turned product rubrics into training signal: graders, human-feedback questions, or preference pairs 

• Cares how Claude behaves for the people using it, not only whether the metric moved 
 The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

 For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

 Annual Salary: $305,000 — $385,000 USD Logistics 
 Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

 Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

 Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

 Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

 Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

 Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

 How we're different 
 We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

 The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

 Come work with us! 
 Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues.  About the Role 

 This is a leadership role, empowering a team of Product Designers. You're bringing together an established Consumer Banking design practice with a newer Business Banking effort for the first time, building the shared rituals and practices that will connect them, while staying close enough to the craft to help both products grow.

 This is a player-coach role, for now — but as Banking grows, this role's balance of hands-on craft versus people leadership will shift over time. That's why we're looking for an experienced, hands-on manager: someone who's managed before and is comfortable working as player-coach, using craft to set the bar high for the team they're growing.

 About the Team 

 Gusto already serves over 500,000 small businesses and pays millions of their employees every month. Wallet puts your team's design decisions in front of a meaningful share of those employees directly, and SMB Banking opens the door to the 6.2 million employers in the US (98% with fewer than 100 employees) and the 550,000 new businesses started every year. Because Gusto already runs payroll for hundreds of thousands of businesses, we can design banking that's connected to pay, cash flow, and hiring from day one. You'll help invent what that looks like.

• Build the rituals, hiring pipeline, and planning cadence that span both Consumer Banking and Business Banking for the first time, formalizing what already exists on Wallet and building from zero for Business Banking. 

• Coach designers working at two different stages at once: one optimizing and scaling something live (Wallet), and one defining something that doesn't exist yet (SMB Banking). 

• Co-create goals and success metrics with product and engineering partners for the team, translating strategy into clear scopes, sequences, and milestones. 

• Raise the bar on Wallet's existing quality standard through critique and review, while defining a new standard from scratch for Business Banking. 

• Stay hands-on: review and sometimes do design work directly on the highest-stakes decisions, especially on SMB Banking's path to beta, while coaching your team toward greater independence over time. 

• Partner as an equal in the EPD trio with Banking's PM and engineering leads on each side, and partner regularly with Risk, Compliance, Legal, Data, and Ops given both products are regulated financial products. 

• Ensure Banking's products fit cohesively into Gusto's broader financial ecosystem, coordinating with design and product counterparts on adjacent pods (like Accounting and Payments) so the customer experience feels connected across surfaces rather than fragmented by internal team boundaries. 

• Build individualized career development plans with each direct report, and adapt your leadership style to the person and the moment. 

• Represent Banking's design needs (headcount, quality investment, tooling) to senior design leadership.

• Experience partnering with Risk, Compliance, or Legal on regulated financial products (KYC/KYB, identity verification, money movement rails, partner bank relationships) is a strong plus.

jobs.description:
Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies—from the world's largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups—use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

 About the team 
 Web Presence and Platform is organized into two pillars, each of which is grouped into pods that focus on the central tenets of Stripe's public mission. The Presence pillar creates industry-leading designs for Stripe's front door surfaces, educating customers about the power of our platform, sharing Stripe's ideas and expertise with the public, and driving adoption. The Platform pillar builds the internal machinery that powers these surfaces, and is responsible for making our websites fast, stable, and easy to update.

 Together we design and build stripe.com and other sites that amount to what is, for many, their first impression of Stripe. As such, WPP offers exciting opportunities to have a major impact on Stripe's success. We want to make every pixel count, we want it to be enthralling, and we want to help other Stripes seamlessly benefit from our systematic work.

 What you'll do 
 As a Design Engineer you will concept, prototype, and build new experiences for our web presence. You'll bring your creativity and expertise to the full range of the Stripe brand, across evergreen pages as well as time-based campaigns. You'll both utilize and contribute to our libraries and design systems, and, when appropriate, work outside established systems to create new digital moments. You'll constantly have in-browser performance in mind, and create abstractions that other designers and engineers consume and build upon.

 All Design Engineers in WPP have a shared commitment to user experience and craft, but each pod has subtly different focus areas. The Collective pod leverages design, animation, and interaction to drive awareness, educate prospective users, and share Stripe's expertise across public surfaces such as Stripe.com, Link, and others. The Expansion pod brings the same creativity and executional rigor to attracting new prospects and driving conversion, focusing on user journeys, interactive and highly polished tools for users, and building targeted experiences for our global users.

 As a Design Engineer on the Collective pod, you will help us continue to drive Stripe.com forward, bringing new experiences to life or refining existing content to inform prospective users about the company and its offerings. You will partner closely with designers, other engineers, and partners to execute and evolve the site, bringing technical craft and creativity to the expansive scope of Stripe's web presence.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Collaborate with our team's designers and partners to both create new experiences for and maintain Stripe.com 

• Work closely with other design engineers, pairing, mentoring, and continually building a culture of excellence 

• Prototype and implement web animations and interaction-heavy product launch materials 

• Build beautiful, best-in-class end-user experiences to solve complex problems 

• Utilize, maintain, and extend our design systems 

• Integrate our web platform with self-serve authoring and experimentation 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 3+ years of relevant web front-end development or creative technology experience at a tech-forward, product-driven company 

• Advanced knowledge of modern HTML and CSS 

• Experience writing clear, elegant code in a team environment 

• A zeal for the web as a storytelling medium, demonstrable through a portfolio of design work and frontend code showcasing design systems, engaging microsites, Figma plugins, webGL experiments, CSS art, or anything else—you tell us 

• Experience designing and building public-facing websites that work elegantly across commonly used browsers and devices 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• A good understanding of the formal elements of design, not just limited to the web and including typography, layout, balance, and proportion 

• Proficiency with React, with a focus on interactions, animation, performance, and polish 

• Experience with A/B testing, synthetic monitoring, or accessibility testing

Who we are 
 About Stripe 
 Stripe is a financial infrastructure platform for businesses. Millions of companies, from the world’s largest enterprises to the most ambitious startups, use Stripe to accept payments, grow their revenue, and accelerate new business opportunities. Our mission is to increase the GDP of the internet, and we have a staggering amount of work ahead. That means you have an unprecedented opportunity to put the global economy within everyone's reach while doing the most important work of your career.

 About the team 
 Stripe Terminal helps businesses extend their online presence into the physical world. Our mission is to make it as easy for businesses to accept in-person payments as the Stripe API has made it for online payments. With Terminal, businesses can create flagship retail experiences, extend their websites to pop-up stores, or enable mobile point-of-sale payments at their next event. All of this is built on the Stripe Payments Platform, so businesses can maintain a single view of customers and sales across online and offline channels.

 Our hardware engineering team in Taiwan designs and builds the physical payment devices at the heart of that experience, including products such as the Stripe Reader S700 and Stripe Reader M2. We are expanding the team and seeking an experienced Senior Mechanical and Industrial Design Engineer who can own both the structural engineering and aesthetic form language of our next generation of payment terminals. This is a blended role. You will be equally comfortable driving design for manufacturability (DFM) for a plastic enclosure and sketching form concepts that express Stripe's design identity in hardware.

 What you'll do 
 You will lead the industrial and mechanical design of next-generation Stripe Terminal payment devices, shaping their form, feel, usability, and structural performance from early concepts through mass production. You will partner with cross-functional teams and suppliers to deliver manufacturable, high-quality hardware, including enclosure design, color, material, and finish specifications, packaging, validation, and production readiness.

 Responsibilities 
 Industrial design 
 

• Lead ideation and concept development through rapid hand sketching, digital sketching, and physical foam or 3D-printed models to explore form factors early in the product lifecycle. 

• Define the visual and tactile design language of Terminal hardware, including proportion, form, surface transitions, button feel, and overall product character. 

• Produce photorealistic product renders using KeyShot or similar tools to communicate design intent to cross-functional teams and executive stakeholders. 

• Define and manage color, material, and finish (CMF) specifications. Work directly with suppliers to qualify target surfaces, textures, and coatings. 

• Manage packaging design, working directly with suppliers to qualify final deliverables and the unboxing experience. 

• Apply ergonomics and human factors principles to ensure products are intuitive and comfortable for a diverse range of users and environments. 

• Maintain visual consistency and brand coherence across the Terminal hardware product family, in alignment with Stripe's design identity. 
 
 Mechanical engineering 
 

• Design mechanical components and assemblies using SolidWorks or Creo, following professional engineering standards. 

• Hands on experience in mechanical designs and drawings, assess manufacturability, and resolve technical problems. 

• Lead and plan problem-solving activities using scientific approaches, such as tolerance analysis, computer-aided engineering (CAE) and finite element method (FEM) simulations, design of experiments (DOE), and physical prototyping. 

• Independently analyze and verify mechanical designs, identify risks, and propose mitigations. 

• Manage bill of materials (BOM) cost and design schedules from a mechanical engineering perspective. 

• Prepare mechanical engineering deliverables, including BOMs, component specifications, and support for failure mode and effects analysis (FMEA) activities. 

• Review Design fixtures and calibration processes for high-precision mechanical assemblies. 

• Verify and qualify components in first-article builds from suppliers, and participate in pilot production. 

• Produce and maintain engineering documents, including specifications, design-for-excellence (DFx) guidelines, technical reports, and gate-review packages. 

• Partner with Quality and Reliability teams to support successful validation outcomes and improve hardware durability standards. 

• Support product compliance and certification activities, including Payment Card Industry (PCI) and regulatory certifications. 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements listed below. If you meet these requirements, we strongly encourage you to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement.

 Minimum requirements 
 

• Bachelor's degree in Mechanical Engineering, Industrial Design, or a closely related field. 

• 8+ years of hands-on product design experience spanning mechanical engineering and industrial design, with a portfolio of consumer or commercial hardware products. This includes experience designing consumer-grade plastic enclosures for handheld products, such as smartphones, tablets, or payment terminals, from concept through mass production. 

• Ability to communicate design concepts through hand or digital sketching at the pace of a design conversation, and experience defining CMF specifications with suppliers. 

• Solid understanding of manufacturing and mechanical production processes, with direct experience taking industrial design concepts through DFM, tooling, and production. 

• Proficiency in mechanical CAD software. Creo is required, and SolidWorks is a plus. Expertise in creating detailed 2D drawings and performing geometric dimensioning and tolerancing (GD&T) and tolerance analysis. 

• Familiarity with mold design, first-article inspection (FAI) processes, and process capability (Cpk) analysis, along with experience managing supplier and factory relationships. 

• Strong written and spoken English and Mandarin communication skills to collaborate directly with suppliers in Taiwan, Hong Kong, and mainland China throughout product development and production. Willingness to travel internationally, including to Hong Kong and mainland China, as needed. 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Proficiency in rendering software, with KeyShot strongly preferred. VRED or Blender experience is also valued. 

• Experience maintaining a coherent design language across a multi-SKU hardware product family or accessory ecosystem. 

• Familiarity with ergonomics methodologies, including grip studies, anthropometric data, and usability evaluations, applied to handheld device design. 

• Experience with point-of-sale hardware, payment terminals, or consumer electronics peripherals. 

• Knowledge of PCI hardware requirements, material properties, and associated manufacturing processes. 

• Proficiency in thermal calculations and an understanding of plastic material properties. 

• Experience with mechanical simulation tools and metal-part design. 

• Ability to create compelling design presentations for cross-functional and executive audiences, clearly articulating the rationale behind design decisions.

We’ll need to persuade people and organisations to change course: labs changing their research paths; entrepreneurs quitting their jobs to start something new; funders reprioritising their grant programs. You’ll laser in on the influential voices, and build targeted strategies to shift opinions and behaviours using traditional media, podcasts, video, substackers, influencers, events, and Twitter. You’ll craft compelling messaging on world-altering technologies; announce billions of dollars worth of grants and investments; publish opinionated editorial designed to inflect research fields; build communities of superfans; and manage coalitions of the world’s biggest companies and philanthropic organizations.  About the team 
 Brand Studio sits at the center of everything Stripe shows the world — from visual identity and brand systems to campaigns, events, digital experiences, and global marketing. The studio functions as a creative multiplier: setting the standards, building the systems, and producing the work that helps Stripe show up with intention and quality across every touchpoint.

 World-class creative output requires world-class operational infrastructure. Brand Operations is the function that makes Brand Studio's work possible at scale — not by managing the execution, but by architecting the conditions that enable it. That means shaping what enters the studio, ensuring clarity before a brief is written, and building the systems that allow creative directors and producers to focus on what they're here to do: create exceptional work.

 What you’ll do 
 Most operations leaders are brought in to fix problems. We're looking for someone who prevents them — and designs the system in which prevention becomes the norm.

 The Head of Brand Operations exists upstream from creative execution. This role's job is to ensure the work entering Brand Studio is strategically aligned, clarified, prioritized, resourced, and fully prepared for delivery before it ever reaches a creative director or producer. It also means ensuring the company understands how to work with Brand Studio — what it takes to be a ready partner, and where a given initiative stands on the roadmap. When that infrastructure is working, creative leaders spend their time and energy on the thing they're actually here to do.

 This role lives at the altitude of setting the team up for success. That means the early-stage, ambiguous conversations where partners are still forming ideas — where the business need hasn't been articulated, where the biggest risks and opportunities haven't been named, and where a structural decision will compound over time. It means building and maintaining a roadmap the entire company can see and trust. And it means leading a team of producers who own their projects fully, with your role being the system that makes their ownership meaningful.

 This role isn't about staying out of the details entirely — it's about not defaulting to them. You'll roll up your sleeves when the moment calls for it. But your primary value is in designing the ecosystem, not running the work. If you want to build the system in which great work consistently becomes possible — and watch it scale — this is a rare opportunity to do that.

 Responsibilities 
 

• Architect the Brand Studio ecosystem. Engage cross-functional partners — Marketing, Product, Comms, PMM — before briefs exist. Turn ambiguous asks into clear, sequenced workstreams so creative leaders inherit clarity, not chaos. 

• Build and maintain the Brand Studio roadmap. Sequence and prioritize work based on business importance, creative opportunity, and team capacity. Give leadership a forward-looking view of what's coming — and the tradeoffs involved. 

• Set the conditions for great work. By the time a project reaches a creative director or producer, the business need is defined, stakeholders are aligned, and the problem is framed. Creative leaders shape the work. You shape the environment that makes the work possible. 

• Own and evolve the operational infrastructure. Build the intake processes, alignment frameworks, and communication rhythms that help Brand Studio run at scale. Refine them as the team grows. 

• Make how Brand Studio works visible to the company. Partners should be able to find the roadmap, understand where their project stands, and know what it takes to show up ready. The process of working with Brand Studio shouldn't require a meeting to explain. 

• Run the business of Brand Studio. Own the budget, manage agency and external production partnerships from procurement through delivery standards, and partner with Finance on clear accounting structures. Give the team the resources and partnerships it needs to deliver. 

• Lead, develop, and set the cultural tone. Hire great people, build their judgment, and set clear ownership. Give direct feedback, delegate fully, and create the stability that lets people do their best work. You're a steward of how this team shows up — the norms, the standards, and what it means to operate at this level. 

• Stay attuned to what's forming. Brand-level initiatives take shape before briefs exist. Catch early signals across the company and help shape ambiguous ideas into clear outcomes before they reach the studio. 

• Represent Brand Studio at the leadership level. Keep senior leaders informed on priorities, direction, and impact. Make the case for what deserves investment, what should wait, and why. 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 12+ years of experience in brand operations, creative operations, or creative program management. A track record of building operational systems at the function level, not just executing inside them. 

• 5+ years managing a team of producers, program managers, or operations professionals, with clear evidence of developing talent and building production capability. 

• Demonstrated experience engaging cross-functional partners before briefs are written — shaping workstreams, clarifying business needs, and setting creative teams up to succeed. 

• Experience building and owning an annual creative roadmap for a team or function, including prioritization frameworks, capacity planning, and tradeoff communication with senior leadership. 

• A track record of building operational infrastructure — intake processes, prioritization systems, partner communication frameworks — that scaled and outlasted your direct involvement. 

• Experience managing significant budgets, including developing transparent accounting structures in partnership with Finance. 

• Strong stakeholder management and executive communication skills, with the ability to align competing priorities and influence without authority across a large, cross-functional organization. 

• People management instincts that build team judgment rather than dependency — genuine delegation, direct feedback, and a consistent bias toward developing others over personal execution. 

• Experience incorporating AI into team workflows and driving measurable adoption across a creative or operations team. 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Experience inside a world-class in-house creative studio or brand team, with deep familiarity with the full creative production lifecycle — from strategy and concept through final delivery. 

• A track record of building or rebuilding a brand operations function from scratch within a company or team at scale. 

• Experience managing global creative agency and external production partnerships end to end — from procurement and onboarding through creative direction and delivery standards. 

• Deep understanding of how brand, marketing, and product teams operate at a technology company, with the instincts to bridge creative ambition and business priorities. 

• Experience building operational transparency systems — roadmaps, dashboards, or partner-facing communication frameworks — that gave an entire organization real-time visibility into a creative team's capacity and priorities.

 About the team 
 The Design team works across most projects at Stripe—from our brand standards to campaigns, events, digital products, and even printed publications. And since Stripe’s main audience is other people who build products, we agonize over and take pride in crafting user-friendly and user-focused experiences.

 The Brand Design team lays the foundations that help Stripe accelerate. We do this by creating, evolving, and maintaining Stripe’s high-quality, versatile, and forward-looking visual identity design system. We sweat the details. We make it seem effortless.

 Our team—and our design efforts—are multipliers for Stripe and Stripes. Our focus on principles, systems, and standards makes it easier for all Stripes to get work done—at a high quality bar, while still creating space for evolution and innovation. Collaborating with other teams at Stripe, as well as select external partners, we raise the quality and consistency of interactions with the Stripe brand.

 Brand Designer leaders at Stripe demonstrate passion for great design and for expanding, evolving, defining, and documenting flexible design systems that achieve bar-raising quality and consistency for the brand at scale. They are user focused, have a strong understanding of the business, and are empathetic and inspiring team leaders. The ideal candidate excels across a variety of styles, crisply articulates design decisions, iterates quickly, and collaborates seamlessly with marketers, product managers, leaders, other designers, and agency partners.

 About the role 
 The headline in a campaign that runs during a game break. The sentence in a developer's first API moment. The story in a 90-second film that makes a fintech company feel like something worth believing in. They all start as an idea, and they all carry the same responsibility: to be precise, surprising, and genuinely worth someone's attention.

 We're looking for a Creative Director, Copy & Campaigns: someone who leads with language, thinks in concepts, and can also think in systems. This isn't a management role that occasionally writes, or a writing role that occasionally leads. It's both, fully. You'll generate the big campaign ideas and write the line that makes them land. You'll help set the creative vision for how Stripe shows up in the world, then stay close enough to the work to make it sharper. You'll direct agency partners without retreating into an approval layer. And you'll do the hard, underrated part of the job: selling the work through. That means building concepts strong enough that leadership buys them, and audiences buy into them.

 You'll also help navigate genuinely new territory: how a category-defining infrastructure company earns a place in culture, not just through product launches, but through the moments that move people. AI is reshaping how creative work gets made, and we're not looking for someone who has it all figured out. We're looking for someone actively and curiously building toward what creativity can become in this moment, and excited to do that here.

 If you want to run work at arm's length, this isn't the role. If you're excited by a role where the quality of your ideas, the sharpness of your copy, and the ambition you bring to the work all matter, this is a place to build.

 What you’ll do 
 

• Own the words. Lead concepting and copy across global campaigns, from the insight that unlocks a campaign to the headline that earns a second look to the narrative that builds the brand. This is a thinking-and-writing role. Consistently, not occasionally. 

• Run campaigns end to end. Turn strategy into a sharp creative concept, then a clear POV, then work that ships across film, OOH, digital, and activations, distinctive at every touchpoint. Take ideas from blank page to bought to live. 

• Get the work bought. Develop concepts that hold up under scrutiny and present them so they win: to senior leadership, to cross-functional partners, and ultimately to the audiences they're built to move. 

• Lead Stripe's partnerships. Build creative strategies and executions that bring Stripe inside culture: sponsorship, storytelling, live moments. 

• Partner with agencies. Collaborate on sharp briefs. Push thinking at the concept stage, not just the polish stage. Give feedback that moves the work forward, and stay close enough to know where it needs to go and how to help it get there. 

• Build with AI, not just alongside it. Experiment actively in how you ideate and write, not to cut corners, but to expand what's possible. Build new workflows. Share what you learn. 

• Make everyone around you sharper. Help writers be more precise, designers find their voice, and marketers think with more creative ambition. Expect the same in return. 

• Shape what Stripe advertising becomes. Be a strong cross-functional voice connecting creative to business goals, user insights, and brand positioning. Raise the team's standards, ambitions, and culture of craft. 
 
 Who you are 
 We're looking for someone who meets the minimum requirements to be considered for the role. If you meet these requirements, you are encouraged to apply. The preferred qualifications are a bonus, not a requirement. 

 Minimum requirements 
 

• 10+ years of experience in copywriting and creative direction, with work that shows strong language craft, strategic thinking, and breakthrough campaign concepts, ideally for product-driven or tech companies. 

• 3+ years of experience managing teams, agencies, or creative partners in high-growth environments, with a clear ability to brief, concept, review, produce, and push work to a higher standard. 

• A portfolio led by ideas, language, and sharp conceptual thinking. You are actively generating concepts, writing, visibly shaping the work, and staying close to the craft. 

• A track record of selling ambitious work through: concepting ideas and presenting them in a way that earns buy-in from stakeholders and senior leadership without diluting them. 

• Strong instincts across film, digital, print, OOH, and activations, with a pulse on culture and the ability to turn insights into concepts that earn attention. 

• A genuine curiosity about AI in the creative process, including active experimentation and an honest perspective on how it can shape how creative work gets made. 

• A strong partnership mindset, especially with producer leads. You work closely together to drive program success, maintain quality, manage alignment, and keep the work moving with clarity. 

• Strong stakeholder management and communication skills, with the ability to navigate ambiguity, align competing priorities, present to senior leadership, and bring people in on the creative. 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• Experience in sports marketing, sponsorship activations, or brand-in-culture work, with a perspective of how brands earn credibility in spaces they don't own. 

• Created concept-led work that generated real cultural traction and conversation, beyond media spend alone. 

• Built or contributed to voice and tone systems, copy standards, or brand language infrastructure. 

• Worked in environments where product and brand both had to work hard, and where the product itself was central to the story. 

• Created award-caliber work, with the perspective to know awards are not always the goal, but they do have an important place in raising ambition, sharpening craft, and building a team's creative standard.

The Presence pillar owns the public-facing storytelling across stripe.com and link.com—including our homepage, product landing pages, industry and solutions pages, and other high-impact go-to-market surfaces. Together, we shape how millions of people understand what Stripe is and what it can do for them.

 Designers on the Presence team work at the intersection of craft and impact—balancing clarity, polish, and systems thinking with strategic storytelling and experimentation. We collaborate closely with engineering, marketing, content, and product to deliver work that is not only beautiful, but measurably moves the business.

 What you'll do 
 As a Designer on the Presence team, you'll own design across two distinct and high-visibility surface areas—Link (the Stripe one-click checkout experience and link.com) and Bridge (bridge.xyz—the Stripe stablecoin financial infrastructure, operating as its own standalone web property). These are some of the most strategically varied and creatively demanding surfaces in our portfolio—each with its own audience, brand voice, and design challenge.

 You'll operate with a high degree of autonomy—driving work from brief to launch, navigating ambiguity with confidence, and setting the quality bar for your focus areas. You'll shape the design systems and storytelling frameworks that make these surfaces scale, and you'll build deep expertise that makes you a go-to partner for the cross-functional teams you work alongside. • Drive clarity in ambiguous or loosely defined briefs by synthesizing user needs, business goals, and technical constraints into a coherent point of view 

• Lead cross-functional collaboration with engineering, PMM, content design, brand, and product—facilitating alignment, integrating feedback, and keeping projects moving 

• Partner deeply with engineering throughout the design process, from exploring technical possibilities and constraints early, to co-creating solutions at the intersection of craft and code, and ensuring design intent carries through to final implementation 

• Develop and advance design systems, patterns, and components specific to your surfaces, ensuring they are extensible and maintainable at scale 

• Apply and evolve visual and interaction standards that uphold the quality bar across diverse surface types—from immersive event experiences to conversion-focused product pages • Use research insights, user testing, and performance data to ground your decisions and advocate for the user across partner conversations

• A strong portfolio demonstrating exceptional visual craft, systems thinking, and the ability to lead complex, multi-faceted design work independently

That's exactly why judgment, taste , and craft matter here in a way they don't in lower-stakes products.

 AI in your workflow. Using AI to explore ideas, prototype, and synthesize research — so you progress faster without losing craft.

 As the Product Designer, Finance, you'll set the UX vision and strategy across four interconnected product areas: Business Money, Consumer Money, Payments, and Risk. Your role is to see what individual teams can't, identifying opportunities and systemic gaps that span the full financial experience, and to drive the work that makes Gusto's financial products feel clear, trustworthy, and empowering for hundreds of thousands of small businesses and their employees. Nobody has fully figured out what AI-first financial UX looks like at scale. This role is the chance to define it at Gusto. This role's level is similar to Senior Staff. 

 Your work will span the full scope: defining a long-term UX vision that connects financial and trust experiences across teams, identifying and driving high-impact opportunities that no single pod could tackle alone, and shaping product strategy alongside product directors and engineering leaders. You'll step in as a direct IC on the highest-priority projects, develop other designers, and contribute platform patterns that scale beyond the Money and Risk teams.

 About the team 

 The Money team builds the financial products that help small businesses and their employees move, manage, and access money—from the tools owners use to run their business finances, to the financial benefits available to their teams. As Gusto deepens its financial ecosystem, this team sits at the center of making money movement faster, simpler, and more empowering for hundreds of thousands of small businesses and the people who work for them.

 The Risk team is the trust layer that makes all of it possible. They build the systems that protect customers and Gusto from fraud and financial exposure, and the identity infrastructure that determines how customers verify who they are and how they access Gusto's financial products. It's foundational work: quiet when it's working, critical when it's not.

 Together, these two teams own one of the broadest and most consequential design scopes at Gusto.

• Set the UX vision and strategy across the Money and Risk teams, connecting the dots across multiple pods and ensuring a cohesive experience throughout the platform. 

• Identify and drive high-impact design opportunities across the Money and Risk teams, spotting what individual pods can't see from inside their area, and bringing the right partners along to pursue them. 

• Influence product strategy, roadmap priorities, and team OKRs across Money and Risk through a design lens—operating as a senior design co-owner alongside product directors and engineering leaders. 

• Define what AI-first financial UX looks like at Gusto, including how to represent uncertainty clearly, surface errors gracefully, preserve user agency when AI recommendations are wrong, and build trust across consequential automated decisions. 

• Own how the Money and Risk teams build and share customer understanding: setting learning priorities, synthesizing insights across pods, and ensuring customer knowledge consistently informs direction rather than sitting siloed within individual teams.

jobs.description:
About Anthropic 
 Anthropic’s mission is to create reliable, interpretable, and steerable AI systems. We want AI to be safe and beneficial for our users and for society as a whole. Our team is a quickly growing group of committed researchers, engineers, policy experts, and business leaders working together to build beneficial AI systems.

 We're looking for a People Specialist to join our People Team. You'll support People Partners and cross functional teams on the work that helps our managers do their jobs well: performance cases, org changes, manager resources, and the operational processes underneath all of it.

 Some weeks you'll be deep in a sensitive performance case coaching a manager. Other weeks you're cleaning up a process, rebuilding a tracker, or helping prep a leader for a hard conversation. We need someone who takes both kinds of work seriously and holds the same quality bar for each.

 A lot of the work is sensitive. You'll be close to performance management, org restructures, and situations that touch ER or Employment Legal. Good judgment about what to share, with whom, and in what form is paramount. 

 Key responsibilities 
 

• 
 Manage performance casework: building documentation, tracking timelines, prepping talking points, and keeping details from falling through the cracks while owning the process end to end 

 

• 
 Own and improve operational processes that managers and People Partners depend on, including outside business activity requests and reorg processing

 

• 
 Build, maintain, and improve manager resources and documentation so they're actually useful and actually current

 

• 
 Partner with Leadership Design on manager enablement programs like the performance cycle: logistics, content, delivery, and the unglamorous operational work that makes programs run

 

• 
 Pull and compile reports and data for sensitive personnel matters 

 

• 
 Maintain tracking systems for casework and manager enablement initiatives; make them better than you found them

 
 
 Minimum qualifications 
 

• 
 You've supported complex or sensitive casework before and can work with partial information, messy handoffs, and tight timelines

 

• 
 You're detail-oriented: you catch things, close loops, and remember where to find crucial information 

 

• 
 Strong written communication. You'll be drafting things leaders use in hard conversations, and you're not precious when they get edited (you used Claude as a guide but not as a final editor)

 

• 
 Good judgment on need-to-know. You think about what to share, with whom, and what goes in writing versus what stays verbal

 

• 
 You'll push back when something's off. You have a point of view and you're comfortable raising concerns with people more senior than you

 

• 
 Comfortable with range. You don't check out on the tedious work or treat it as beneath you

 
 
 Preferred qualifications 
 

• 
 5+ years in an HR- role: people operations, HR coordination, HRBP, or similar

 

• 
 Experience at a high-growth tech company where process was being built

 

• 
 Direct experience supporting HRBPs, Managers and Employees through challenging and sensitive matters

 

• 
 Working knowledge of HR compliance requirements

 

• 
 Interest in AI safety

 

• 
 Claude power user in your current role

 
 The annual compensation range for this role is listed below. 

 For sales roles, the range provided is the role’s On Target Earnings ("OTE") range, meaning that the range includes both the sales commissions/sales bonuses target and annual base salary for the role.

 Annual Salary: $235,000 — $300,000 USD Logistics 
 Minimum education: Bachelor’s degree or an equivalent combination of education, training, and/or experience

 Required field of study: A field relevant to the role as demonstrated through coursework, training, or professional experience

 Minimum years of experience: Years of experience required will correlate with the internal job level requirements for the position

 Location-based hybrid policy: Currently, we expect all staff to be in one of our offices at least 25% of the time. However, some roles may require more time in our offices.

 Visa sponsorship: We do sponsor visas! However, we aren't able to successfully sponsor visas for every role and every candidate. But if we make you an offer, we will make every reasonable effort to get you a visa, and we retain an immigration lawyer to help with this.

 We encourage you to apply even if you do not believe you meet every single qualification. Not all strong candidates will meet every single qualification as listed. Research shows that people who identify as being from underrepresented groups are more prone to experiencing imposter syndrome and doubting the strength of their candidacy, so we urge you not to exclude yourself prematurely and to submit an application if you're interested in this work. We think AI systems like the ones we're building have enormous social and ethical implications. We think this makes representation even more important, and we strive to include a range of diverse perspectives on our team.

 Your safety matters to us. To protect yourself from potential scams, remember that Anthropic recruiters only contact you from @anthropic.com email addresses. In some cases, we may partner with vetted recruiting agencies who will identify themselves as working on behalf of Anthropic. Be cautious of emails from other domains. Legitimate Anthropic recruiters will never ask for money, fees, or banking information before your first day. If you're ever unsure about a communication, don't click any links—visit anthropic.com/careers directly for confirmed position openings.

 How we're different 
 We believe that the highest-impact AI research will be big science. At Anthropic we work as a single cohesive team on just a few large-scale research efforts. And we value impact — advancing our long-term goals of steerable, trustworthy AI — rather than work on smaller and more specific puzzles. We view AI research as an empirical science, which has as much in common with physics and biology as with traditional efforts in computer science. We're an extremely collaborative group, and we host frequent research discussions to ensure that we are pursuing the highest-impact work at any given time. As such, we greatly value communication skills.

 The easiest way to understand our research directions is to read our recent research. This research continues many of the directions our team worked on prior to Anthropic, including: GPT-3, Circuit-Based Interpretability, Multimodal Neurons, Scaling Laws, AI & Compute, Concrete Problems in AI Safety, and Learning from Human Preferences.

 Come work with us! 
 Anthropic is a public benefit corporation headquartered in San Francisco. We offer competitive compensation and benefits, optional equity donation matching, generous vacation and parental leave, flexible working hours, and a lovely office space in which to collaborate with colleagues. Guidance on Candidates' AI Usage: Learn about our policy for using AI in our application process.

Building at Webflow takes grit because we move fast without sacrificing craft or quality.

 We're looking for a Senior Communications Manager who can help tell that story wherever it matters most.

 You'll work closely with our Director of Communications and Communications Lead, owning internal communications programs while contributing across executive and external communications based on the team's priorities.

 You might write a message for one of our senior leaders one day, help develop talking points for an executive appearance the next, and then jump into communications for a major product or company announcement. You'll work closely with our Director of Communications and Communications Lead, shifting between internal, executive, and external communications based on what's most important for Webflow at the time.

 We're looking for someone who is an excellent writer, a strong operator, and comfortable moving between very different kinds of communications work. You should be able to take a complicated brief, quickly understand what matters, and turn it into something people want to read.

 About the role: 

 

• Location: Remote-first (United States) 

• Full-time 

• Permanent 

• Exempt 

• The cash compensation for this role is tailored to align with the cost of labor in different geographic markets. We've structured the base pay ranges for this role into zones for our geographic markets, and the specific base pay within the range will be determined by the candidate’s geographic location, job-related experience, knowledge, qualifications, and skills.

• Zone B: $141,500 - $170,000

 This role is also eligible to participate in Webflow's company-wide bonus program. Target amounts are a percentage of base salary and vary by career level. Payouts are based on company performance against established financial and operational goals. 

 Please visit our Careers page for more information on which locations are included in each of our geographic pay zones. However, please confirm the zone for your specific location with your recruiter.

 

• Application Information: 
 

• Application deadline: applications accepted on an ongoing basis until position is closed and filled 

• This posting is for an existing vacancy 
 

• Reporting to the Director, Communications

• Own the day-to-day execution of Webflow's internal communications program, including company-wide announcements, our internal editorial calendar, and recurring communications. 

• Lead planning and production for major company moments, including monthly All Team meetings, Webflow Kick Off (WKO), and other company-wide events. 

• Write and edit communications for Webflow executives across internal and external moments, including employee messages, talking points, presentations, speeches, and other executive communications. 

• Support major company and product announcements, working with the Director of Communications and Communications Lead to turn communications strategies into strong execution. 

• Work across People, EPD, Revenue, Marketing, Finance, Legal, and other teams to gather context, develop communications, and keep high-priority work moving. 

• Support company changes with communications plans, FAQs, manager materials, leadership messaging, and follow-up communications. 

• Jump into other communications work when priorities shift, including executive prep, research, messaging, external communications, and special projects. 

• Own and improve the systems behind our internal communications, including our editorial calendar, intake process, playbooks, and publishing workflows. 

• Use AI to reduce manual work, move faster, and spend more time on the communications work that requires context and judgment. 
 
 About you: 

 Requirements:

 

• 7+ years of experience in corporate communications, internal communications, executive communications, PR, or a related communications role, ideally at a high-growth technology company. 

• Exceptional writer and editor who can move comfortably between different voices, audiences, and formats. 

• Strong communications judgment, particularly when working with sensitive, incomplete, or fast-moving information. 

• Experience working directly with senior leaders and turning messy or complicated inputs into strong communications. 

• Experience running communications programs, company-wide meetings, launches, or other high-visibility moments. 

• Strong project management skills and the ability to keep multiple workstreams moving at once. 

• Strong cross-functional skills and experience working across teams such as Product, Sales, Marketing, People, Finance, and Engineering. 

• Experience working in remote or distributed organizations. 
 
 You’ll thrive as a Senior Communications Manager if you:

 

• Want meaningful ownership and the chance to become a stronger, more well-rounded communications leader. 

• Love to write and care about making communications clear, engaging, and human. 

• Enjoy learning new parts of the business and turning what you learn into great communications. 

• Are organized, dependable, and comfortable managing several projects at once. 

• Are curious about how AI is changing communications and actively look for ways to use it to work smarter and improve the work. 
 
 Our Core Behaviors: 

 

• Build lasting customer trust. We build trust by taking action that puts customer trust first. 

• Win together. We play to win, and we win as one team. Success at Webflow isn't a solo act. 

• Reinvent ourselves. We don't just improve what exists, we imagine what's possible. 

• Own it all the way. We move fast because the moment demands it, and we hold ourselves accountable to deliver outcomes — for each other, and for customers. 
 
 Benefits

• Health coverage that actually covers you. Comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans for full-time employees and their dependents, with Webflow covering most premiums. 

• Support for every stage of family life . 12 weeks of paid parental leave for all parents and 6+ weeks of additional paid leave for birthing parents. Plus inclusive care for family planning, menopause, and midlife transitions. 

• Time off that’s actually off. Flexible vacation, paid holidays, and a sabbatical program to help you recharge and come back inspired.

• Invest in your future. A 401(k) with 100% employer match (up to $6,000/year) in the U.S., and support for retirement savings globally. 

• Monthly stipends that flex with your life. Localized support for work and wellness expenses — from Wi-Fi to workouts.

 Be you, with us

We are an Equal Opportunity (EEO)/Veterans/Disabled Employer and are committed to building an inclusive global team that represents a variety of backgrounds, perspectives, beliefs, and experiences. Upon interview scheduling, instructions for accommodation requests will be administered.

 About the Role: 
 We're looking for a Visual Designer to join our Website Design Engineering team. Your home base is Vercel's web presence, vercel.com , nextjs.org , product launches, and Ship, where you'll design pages, systems, and interactions that get built and shipped, not just handed off. But the impact is bigger than the site: you'll shape how the Vercel brand shows up in the world, from launch moments and event experiences to motion, illustration, and brand-partnership surfaces across digital and physical mediums. You'll work shoulder-to-shoulder with design engineers who turn design into production code, so your work lives on the real web at Vercel's bar for polish. 

 This is a role for a designer who thinks in systems and sweats the details: someone equally at home setting the typographic rhythm of a landing page, and shaping how a tier-one hero feels on first load.

 First and foremost, this is a visual design role. Exceptional creativity and design craft for the web are what matter most. Our design engineers own turning design into production code, and you're encouraged to get hands-on in the medium yourself and carry an idea all the way to production when you want to. Either way, we're hiring you for your eye and your ideas, and coding is never a requirement. You will report to the Director of Website Design Engineering and can be remote or hybrid across our SF, NY, London, or Berlin hubs.

 

 If you’re based within a pre-determined commuting distance of one of our offices (SF, NY, London, or Berlin), the role includes in-office anchor days on Monday, Tuesday, and Friday. If you're located beyond that distance, the role is fully remote. For location-specific details, please connect with our recruiting team.

 What You Will Do: 
 

• Define the visual language of Vercel's most-seen surfaces, vercel.com , nextjs.org , product launches, and Ship, and set a creative direction the whole team builds from. 

• Create the moments people remember: hero animations, launch films, event environments, and brand-partnership work that reaches across screen and physical space. 

• Own the creative vision end to end, from the first spark of a concept to the finished result shipped on the real web, alongside design engineers who turn your work into production code. 

• Set the craft bar: the typography, motion, and detail that make a page unmistakably Vercel, the kind of work other teams measure themselves against. 

• Move fluidly across mediums, web, motion, illustration, 3D, and identity, and raise the bar wherever the Vercel brand shows up. 

• Leave a mark on the system: influence Geist and our shared patterns through work good enough to become the standard. 
 
 
 About You: 
 

• Above all, a distinctive eye and original ideas. Exceptional visual design instincts and creativity are the heart of this role, and the web is where most of your work will live. 

• A portfolio spanning brand systems and work across multiple digital and physical mediums, anchored by strong, shipped web work. 8+ years of design experience. 

• Meaningful hands-on range across several of these: motion, 3D, illustration, environmental and event design, and interaction. This is a maker's role, and coding is not what we mean by hands-on. 

• Systems-minded: you design components and patterns, not one-offs, and think about how each choice fits a broader system. 

• You've shaped launch moments, events, or brand-partnership surfaces under real deadlines, and you know how to make a moment land. 

• You thrive collaborating with engineers and understand the web as a medium: how layouts behave, what's buildable, how design becomes code. 

• Comfortable in a technology-driven environment; experience with developer, B2B, or SaaS products is a plus. 

• A self-starter and egoless collaborator who takes feedback well and gives it generously. 

• Familiar with Vercel, with working knowledge or experience preferred. 
 
 Bonus If You: 
 

• Can prototype or bring ideas to life in code (React / Tailwind / Next.js). 

• Have contributed to a design system at scale (even if owning ours won't be your job).

• Competitive compensation package, including equity. 

• Inclusive Healthcare Package. 

• Learn and Grow - we provide mentorship and send you to events that help you build your network and skills.

• We will provide you the gear you need to do your role, and a WFH budget for you to outfit your space as needed.

jobs.description:
Figma is growing our team of passionate creatives and builders on a mission to make design accessible to all. Figma’s platform helps teams bring ideas to life—whether you're brainstorming, creating a prototype, translating designs into code, or iterating with AI. From idea to product, Figma empowers teams to streamline workflows, move faster, and work together in real time from anywhere in the world. If you're excited to shape the future of design and collaboration, join us!

 Figma is building its founding Forward Deployed Engineering team to solve the complex, real-world challenges that emerge when bringing Figma’s products into large-scale enterprise environments and looking for founding Forward Deployed Engineers. As a Forward Deployed Engineer, you’ll embed directly with strategic customers, working across their codebases, design systems, developer environments, and workflows to make Figma’s products successful within their unique technical constraints. You’ll tackle the hardest adoption challenges hands-on, from complex frontend stacks and legacy systems to security and access requirements, while building trusted partnerships with customers’ senior engineering teams.

 This is a senior/staff-level engineering role within Product and Engineering, not a sales or services function. You’ll work directly in customer environments when needed, using the minimum access required. Your goal is smooth adoption by the customer’s product and engineering teams, which means making complex workflows work simply in their environment and solving the underlying problems You’ll do that hands-on, often by writing Figma product code, then turn what you learn into a reusable path for future customers instead of taking permanent ownership of the customer’s codebase. . Working closely with Figma’s Product, Engineering, Sales, and Customer Experience teams, you’ll help shape both the product and how this brand-new function works and scales. The role is highly collaborative, deeply customer-facing, and built for engineers who thrive in ambiguity, take end-to-end ownership, and want to solve the highest-impact problems at the intersection of product, engineering, and customer needs. This role includes periodic travel to work alongside strategic customers in person.

 This is a full time role that can be held from one of our US hubs or remotely in the United States.

 What you'll do at Figma: 
 

• Make an enterprise design system agent-ready so AI tools generate faithful, on-system code: fix tokens, naming, and guidelines, wire up Code Connect, and run evals. 

• Get Make Local, Code Layers, and our newest products working in a customer’s real environment, writing code, config, agent skills, and guideline files against their systems and ours. 

• Run technical discovery: understand a customer's dev environment, toolchain, and constraints, then scope the fastest credible path to value, in addition to setting the customer up for long term success. 

• Debug hard, unfamiliar integration problems (git workflows, CI, dev-environment setup, non-standard stacks). 

• Build LLM-powered workflows: MCP setup, agent skills, and prompt engineering tuned to each customer’s context. 

• Turn one-off solutions into reusable playbooks and product feedback, so patterns you solve once become self-serve or shipped product. 

• Bring learnings on friction back to Figma's Product and Engineering teams, influence what gets built next, and often build it. 
 
 We'd love to hear from you if you have: 
 

• 5+ years shipping production software end-to-end, with meaningful time embedded with customers or partner teams. 

• Excellent customer-facing communication and technical partnership skills, with the ability to build trust with senior engineers and translate customer needs into actionable product and engineering solutions 

• Strong engineering fundamentals and adaptability, with the ability to quickly navigate unfamiliar codebases, languages, and technical environments to deliver production-ready solutions. 

• Hands-on experience with design systems and design-to-code workflows, including component libraries, tokens, documentation, and the tooling that connects design artifacts to production code. 

• Proficiency in TypeScript/JavaScript or Python, including demonstrated fluency with agentic coding tools (e.g., MCP, agent orchestration). You have hands-on experience integrating APIs and SDKs, troubleshooting toolchains and CI environments, and navigating enterprise requirements such as SSO, security reviews, access controls, data residency, and compliance frameworks. 

• Comfort owning ambiguous technical problems end to end, identifying patterns across customer engagements, and turning field learning into reusable product improvements. 
 
 While it's not required, it's an added plus if you also have: 
 

• Background in forward-deployed engineering, solutions engineering, professional services, developer experience, or a similar customer-facing technical role 

• Familiarity with developer tools, design-to-code workflows, or AI/LLM products, including tools such as Code Connect, Storybook, Style Dictionary, or comparable technologies 

• Proven ability to partner cross-functionally with Sales, Customer Experience, Solutions Architecture, or related teams to deliver complex enterprise engagements

If you’re excited about this role but your past experience doesn’t align perfectly with the points outlined in the job description, we encourage you to apply anyways. You may be just the right candidate for this or other roles.
